body:
I was initially suspicious that this was just a bad interaction between `BoneAttachment3D::override_pos` and `SkeletonModifier3D`, since that combination is noted as unsupported in the docs. However, after looking into it further, you can actually reproduce the same issue without `BoneAttachment3D` at all.

You can reproduce the behavior difference by doing anything that marks the skeleton as dirty while the game is paused. Here's [an MRP](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21925361/MRP.zip) that pauses the game after a few frames, and then adds a new bone to the skeleton the frame after that. When the new bone gets added, the skeleton gets marked as dirty, which updates the skeleton based on the global pose only, without modifiers.

The core issue stems from [these three lines of the change](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103639/files#diff-15517aa247c8a98fa4c614038028e6e9d9179e3476c20f3af3fd41816b458611L360-R362) that avoids calling `_process_modifiers` unless the modifiers are marked as updated. The `Skeleton3D::make_dirty` method ends up getting called in a variety of situations, but it only passes `UPDATE_FLAG_POSE`, not `UPDATE_FLAG_MODIFIER`, so the modifiers end up getting skipped in those code paths.

If the skeleton gets dirtied, I think it makes sense to update the modifiers as well as the pose, and if you do so this regression is fixed.
